utterances.text: I'm asking you, was it both of them or just one of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Show the witness Exhibit P431, would you? May I explain this to you, sir? You are being cross-examined, and it is necessary for the purposes of cross-examination to direct your attention to the evidence you gave. You are not being asked simply to repeat things. You are being asked questions about what you said yesterday. So it's no use you repeatedly complaining that you are being asked to say the same thing time and again. Now, is that 431, is it? If you could identify on that document which one you are now being asked about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I haven't seen the document. Has it got numbers on it? Does it? Are these the numbers from the list, are they? Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you please tell us when did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that I cannot -- that I do not remember dates but he repeated it to me over and over again, that one and the other one on the list, but this one more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the other one who is on the list also told you that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you for the date, but could you roughly, between -- as of the time when you got to the KP Dom, when roughly, how much later did he tell you that? Can you tell us that, roughly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a few months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yesterday, you said that you had worked -- not of our own free will. Did all the other prisoners have to follow orders and work under such orders?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that I said yesterday I repeat today, so you want me to answer this too? I personally was persecuted and made to work and I remember how I was lying down, I couldn't work any longer from exhaustion, and Savo Todovic kicked me with his feet to make me go to work. I am speaking about other people, younger people, who could be my sons, that they wailed for a piece of bread, for a crust of bread. That is people were at the end of their tether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just stop. You are repeating what you said yesterday but you are not answering the question. The question was: Did all the other prisoners have to follow orders and work under such orders? Now, we don't want to hear about your own experiences again. Just answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question that was put to me, there was one period when the young men thought, "Well, let's go to work," and that was voluntary, whereas all the other periods when people were made to go and work in the mine and made to work outside, people tried to hide away, but they couldn't help it because if you did not carry out orders, you were done for. So that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In which period did you work in the mine?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me answer. Again I don't know the date. But I worked for three to four days. I had a wound on my leg. The assumption was that it was cancer. I was crying, begging every day, and I even asked the Red Cross about this but this was almost when I was about to leave, so they freed me from that obligation. But then immediately after that, they kicked me into the woods to chop wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, sir -- I hope the Honourable Judges won't mind. May I interrupt the witness to make things as short as possible? I just asked the witness when he was taken there to work. So is this the -- towards the end of 1994, because you said that that was before your detention ended.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krnojelac was still warden.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you who the warden was.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember because Sekulovic, Zoran Sekulovic was warden towards the end of 1994, so I think you are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Stop. I was stopping you, Mr. Bakrac, because the translation was still coming through, well and truly. That's not an answer to the question. The question was: Was it towards the end of 1994, because you said it was before your detention ended. Now, are you able to say yes or no to that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Work in the mine was not a month or two before I was released. Perhaps it was earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How much earlier, if you may recall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a few months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So that is in 1994?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm saying before this Court that I do not remember dates because of all the suffering I've been through. These dates were not that important to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know when Sekulovic replaced Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a few months before the exchange, before the exchange of that group of 53 inmates, a few months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What does that mean, a few months, approximately? Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a few, I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was it in 1994?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, towards the end, towards the end. That's when he replaced him, when Sekulovic replaced Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Towards the end of what?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we were released. I can't say now, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I tell you, sir, that he replaced Krnojelac one year and four months before that, do you allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I allow for anything that you say, because all the dates you know are better than what I know, in terms of dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you worked on felling trees and loading wood. Where was that wood being taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were felling trees and the wood was taken to the KP Dom camp, and also to some of the guards in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have furnaces in the living rooms at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date. As for the furnaces, as for the furnaces, we got them through the Red Cross sometimes toward the end of that winter perhaps. All of it was so long. The Red Cross tried and tried and tried, and they finally allowed that, but with great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were these furnaces operating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned that the Red Cross came to the KP Dom. When did the Red Cross come to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Cross tried at the beginning of the war to get into the KP Dom; however, the extremist groups said that nothing international suited them. So the Red Cross came for the first time six months later. It is only six months later that they managed to get into the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Six months after you were detained?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep telling you, I'm never very accurate, I mean, not even in terms of years, but I know it's six months. It's very difficult for me to communicate this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the members of the Red Cross could not see that you were exhausted.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that they could not see that they were exhausted? Well, they were surprised when they saw us. They were surprised to see how exhausted we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you address them? Did you say that you were hungry? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat once again before this Honourable Court what I kept repeating yesterday as well. The people who spoke to the Red Cross about this and that and the other thing, about all these problems that were in the camp, these people would go missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you talk about these problems?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end, before being released from the camp, we said that they were hiding our people, that we didn't know what to do any more, that we were at our wits end and also that our bodies were crumbling. That's personally what I said too, and I was not killed nevertheless. And I can thank this girl from Trebinje, this interpreter who was there, but she was crying, although she was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this six months after your detention?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The end of your detention?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of my detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke of an incident when a Vojvoda entered the KP Dom and slapped Rasim in the face. That's what you said. And then you said to him to stop. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did understand me correctly and that is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you dared tell a Serb Vojvoda to stop slapping Rasim?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: These Serb Vojvodas, when you would stand with them, I mean, those whom you knew, you would say that they were good men, but those Vojvodas, what they did, what they torched, what they killed, that is inconceivable. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I know that Vojvoda from the civilian days, so I took the liberty of asking him to do that, no matter what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since you knew him from the civilian times, can you tell us who he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two brothers from Montenegro. One -- I mean, both worked at the construction company. They came to (redacted) a countless number of times, I mean, this enterprise where I worked, that is. So I can't. I can't say with 100 per cent certainty what their surname was. I knew it for a while, but I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke of another incident when military persons entered the KP Dom and you saw them beating detainees.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever state that somewhere else before?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This incident occurred within the camp compound, inside, because there were two gates sealing off the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In which part of the compound?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the canteen where people went to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few soldiers. I don't know the exact number now. You keep saying "soldiers," but it's extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Or Chetniks. Do you want me to put that way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chetniks and extremists is the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who they hit then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I was pretty far away in the same yard, and I tried to make myself invisible because I knew that they would take people out and kill them. We tried to make ourselves invisible. We hid in some kind of basement there of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you hid, that you did not see this incident?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the beginning of the incident, because what would have made me hide had I not seen the beginning of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So who did they hit at the beginning of this incident?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm telling you I was pretty far away. I mean, I saw Dr. Berberkic, sort of his silhouette, but I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty before this Court that it was him. It looked like a silhouette, and then the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that you escaped to a basement. Where was this basement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basement of the furniture factory, the premises down there. I mean -- well, ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir. What were the hygienic conditions at the KP Dom like?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hygienic conditions at the KP Dom were excellent, what we did, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Did you have medical care at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the KP Dom, the only medical care came from a medical technician. I am convinced that he did not know what the name of various pills was let alone work as a physician.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that this medical technician has had a pharmacy of his own for the past ten years and even more than that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in town?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. Perhaps he has a pharmacy now, but when I was there, no way. I mean, our people say -- our people put it this way: He's the kind of person who would steal everything, all the medicines he had at the KP Dom, and then open the pharmacy of your own. You can do all sorts of things to people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, did physicians from the medical centre in Foca come to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medical care, well, it appeared to be so, but let me explain how they worked. A young man's ulcer perforated and this young man had to be transferred to hospital. No way. No way. The young man died. That is the kind of medical care we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did this young man die in his room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So he died in the room in the prison camp?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As a consequence of his ulcer?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a consequence of his ulcer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was he in your room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not in my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How can you be sure then that he was not taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was moaning and moaning and begging to be taken to hospital, but they did not take him to hospital and he died. He was saying that his ulcer had perforated, but these were not people who would speak English or French or some other language like that that he did not understand them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: There were witnesses here, sir, who said that this person was taken to hospital and that he died in hospital. I'm asking you: Are you sure that he died in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that he moaned and that he was begging. Well, maybe they took him to the hospital when he was dead. However, when it actually happened to him, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you hear his moans?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. We -- we did hear it because everything is nearby. You can hear all these moans. Everything is there. Nothing is far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which room was he in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know in which part of prison?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in one of those first rooms, I think. I think. These were the beginnings, so when I saw everything that was going on -- I mean, it is strange to me nowadays that you put this question to me. Those were the beginnings then. It is strange to me that you ask me whether doctors came. They did come, yes, when the Red Cross was there, so then that it would seem that everything was fine. So I find this question strange. And so many people are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke of an incident when a person escaped. I'm just checking whether we can mention the name of this person. Ekrim Zekovic. I think we can mention the name. Did you see Ekrim Zekovic in the compound?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeated that yesterday. I saw him when he was caught and brought to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, you said -- I don't have to read all of it but it relates to the Zekovic incident: "The next night, the fugitive seemed to have been found. In the morning, we were informed about this." And you were in an isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So here you say that you were told that it seemed that the fugitive had been found and that you were informed about this.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was caught, when this particular person was caught, and before that, that same night, we were told, I mean, after all the beatings and battery, that next day you would be shot dead if he's not found. When he was found, again I'm telling you, the guards who were in the camp, not all of them, one came and said, "You won't be shot dead. He's been found."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you remained in an isolation cell for another 12 days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in the isolation cell. I'm including that night as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That means that you did not see Ekrem Zekovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When everybody was taken out of all the rooms, we were taken out of the isolation cells as well. There were some others there too. We were all taken out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So this is 12 days later when you did your time in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was not after 12 days. It was on the next day. Again I'm telling you I cannot say whether it was yesterday or the day before yesterday. At any rate, within those two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that they were boasting as to how humane they were. Were there any visible wounds on Ekrem Zekovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he have any clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this person can talk about the chains and how he was hit and everything. Let that person talk about it himself. But on the head you couldn't see anything, and I sort of thought, well, I got into more trouble than he did, but he was beaten more in the lower part than I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So when you saw him -- when you saw him, you could not notice anything, whether he had been beaten or not?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why did you not say anywhere, in any one of your statements - and you gave four statements - that Todovic addressed Krnojelac and that he kept nodding and confirming that when he was making this speech?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I not said that, how come you would be telling me that now? Or is this your opinion that I was supposed to have said it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look, sir, you are not helping yourself at all. In fact, you are going a long way to destroying any value that your evidence can have. You are asked a very simple question: Did you tell the OTP investigators about this incident where Mr. Krnojelac nodded as Mr. Todovic addressed the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But they didn't write it down?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Also, you said that all preparations for speeches came from the administration. How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a businessman for a long time, but even if I had been nothing, everything that happens within a firm, everything comes from the administration. Whatever happened in the camp came from the administration of the camp. Any man would know that. It's absurd to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Tell me, when this incident with Zekovic occurred, were you in the same room as he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of this incident, we were next door to one another in the same hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which room was this, which number?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, numbers, no, no. This was on the first floor, upstairs, that room, and then there was this other room, of those who were sort of isolated, those they didn't want to show to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this a working room, the one they didn't want to show the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All rooms -- I mean, this room and that room, and all the rooms. I mean, there were lists, such and such and such a person would go to room -- so persons from all rooms had to go and work. So it's not that one was a working room and another one was not a working room. All of this was done on orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And these persons that they were hiding from the International Red Cross, they were in the left part of the building when you look from the direction of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the building, in the same building, but in a separate room, to the right. To the right is where we were, lots of us. Actually, when you enter on the left, then they were on the right, in a smaller room. I don't know how many they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be easier if I asked the usher to help to give the witness this chart of the KP Dom so that he can show us in which room he was and in which room Zekovic was and in which room those persons that they were hiding from the International Red Cross were.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does this matter? I have no idea. This is the first building. This is the second building, number 2. We were in this building. This is where the ground floor was, and then there was upstairs. Then the ground floor, and then there were two shorter rooms and two longer rooms -- I mean, not shorter and longer but bigger and smaller. And then they were -- I mean when we go upstairs, here, here, somewhere around here. Now, I don't know exactly. Here, here. They were near us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness is indicating building A on the left, the first floor, and the last floor in the same building. Concerning those persons, if I understood things correctly, the witness referred to persons that were being hidden from the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These persons had a separate room. These persons had a separate room, the ones who were being hidden from the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that he was necessarily pointing to the top floor. He said "upstairs." But anyway, we will resume on this subject, no doubt, tomorrow morning. We are very grateful to the court personnel for sitting on with us today so that we can at least get some hours in. We will adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
